guideTitle: Best Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kits Under $300 (2026)
metaTitle: Best Drill Driver Combo Kits Under $300
metaDescription: Five drill and impact driver combo kits at or under $300 compared on motor type, battery count and platform, from Milwaukee M18 to CRAFTSMAN V20.
expertTake: The Milwaukee 2892-22CT is the pick for most buyers because brushless motors, two batteries and a compact frame come in a kit that grows into a very large platform. The BLACK+DECKER BD2KITCDCRL is the value pick for a household that drills and drives a few times a month and does not need brushless. Skip a two-tool kit entirely if you already own batteries from a platform, because bare tools cost less than a bundle. The extra budget over a basic kit mostly buys brushless motors and a second battery, which is where the real daily difference lies.
introParagraphs: A combo kit bundles a drill driver and an impact driver with batteries and a charger, so the question is no longer which tool but which battery family you are committing to. The headline price covers a pair of tools and a charger, but the quality of the batteries and motors varies far more than the box suggests.

This guide explains what the upper end of a modest kit budget actually buys, which features justify the extra money and which marketing numbers to ignore. The picks are listed above, with the reviews below. Listing prices move, and the cap reflects prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Milwaukee 2892-22CT M18 Compact Brushless Drill and Impact Kit

specList.label: Design
specList.value: Compact for overhead and tight spaces

products.description:
Both tools in this kit use brushless motors, which spin without carbon brushes and let the batteries last longer between charges. The compact frames are shorter than full-size drills, so they reach between joists and inside cabinets. Two batteries mean one can charge while the other works.

Compared with the DEWALT DCK240C2, which uses a more traditional motor design, the Milwaukee is built for daily use. It is the strongest platform choice in the roundup because M18 batteries power a vast number of other tools, from saws to lights to vacuums. You pay for that when buying a kit, but the packs can later feed tools that cost far more than this bundle.

Ownership favors people who plan to keep buying. Keep batteries between half charge and full, store them indoors and clean the chuck jaws after drywall work. Replace the drill's clutch ring grease only if it grinds, which is rare. A practical test of any kit at this level is the first full day: two compact batteries typically cover a day of cabinet hanging or trim work, but a day of deck building will drain both, so a spare pack becomes the first accessory worth buying. The impact driver in this kit also earns its place when you meet stubborn fasteners, because the rotational hammering frees rusted or overtightened screws that would strip in a plain drill.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a premium compact kit and plan to build a larger tool collection.

products.name: DEWALT DCK277D2 20V MAX Drill and Impact Driver Kit
products.description:
This kit centers on a compact 7.6 inch design that fits between studs and joists. An LED with a 20-second trigger-release delay keeps the work area lit after you let go, which matters in dark attics or under sinks. An ergonomic grip balances the tool for long sessions.

It competes closely with the Milwaukee M18 kit but sits lower in relative price, and the bag is a practical extra that keeps the tools and batteries together. Versus the DCK240C2, this model is the more compact and modern bundle. If you want DEWALT specifically, this is the one to buy.

Ownership is easy. Both tools use 20V MAX batteries, which work across a wide family of DEWALT tools. Use the bag to protect the chuck from dust, and charge batteries before long jobs. The bag matters more than it sounds, because bare tools tossed in a truck bed or closet pick up dust that works into the chuck and the battery contacts. If you also own an older 20V MAX tool, check that its packs fit the charger in this kit, since the same family charges across generations.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 RP Brushless Drill and Impact Driver Kit
products.description:
This kit brings brushless motors to a lower price tier than Milwaukee and DEWALT, which is its main selling point. The drill spins up to 1,900 RPM, a competitive figure for a compact tool, and the impact driver is described as 27 percent shorter than its predecessor. Two batteries and a charger ship in the box.

The compromise is platform breadth. V20 tools exist but not at the scale of DEWALT or Milwaukee, so future purchases are less flexible. Against the BLACK+DECKER kit, this one gains brushless efficiency and a faster drill. Against the Milwaukee, it saves money but sacrifices ecosystem size.

Ownership is simple. Charge batteries before big jobs and keep the chucks clean. Because the platform is narrower, check that the tools you want later exist in V20 before committing. The practical difference you will feel against the Milwaukee kit is price discipline: you give up a larger ecosystem and gain a lower entry cost, and that tradeoff only matters if you buy more tools later.
products.bestFor: Budget-conscious buyers who want brushless motors without a premium platform.

products.name: DEWALT DCK240C2 20V MAX Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kit
products.description:
UWO, or unit watts out, is DEWALT's measure of power delivered at the chuck, and this kit quotes up to 300. That is a respectable figure for a pair of compact tools, and both fit into hard-to-reach spots. The kit is a long-running DEWALT bundle that many owners picked up as their first set.

The tradeoff is that the listing does not claim brushless motors, so runtime and durability lag the Milwaukee 2892-22CT and the CRAFTSMAN RP. The DCK277D2 is the newer and more compact bundle. If you find this kit at a lower relative price, it makes sense for light use.

Ownership is typical of DEWALT. The batteries share the 20V MAX family, so you can add tools later. Keep the chuck clean, avoid leaving batteries in a hot car and replace dull bits regularly. Because this bundle predates the compact DCK277D2, its tools are slightly longer and its batteries may be older chemistry in some listings, so confirm the pack included when ordering. A kit like this still suits garage projects, fence repair and furniture assembly well.
products.bestFor: Light users who want an established DEWALT kit at a lower relative price.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BD2KITCDCRL 20V MAX Drill and Impact Driver Kit
products.description:
The drill driver has a 3/8 inch chuck and an 11-position clutch, which stops the motor before a screw is overdriven. The variable-speed trigger lets you start slowly, so a bit does not skate across the surface. This is a light-duty kit aimed at household projects.

Compared with the CRAFTSMAN RP kit, this one has no brushless motors and fewer batteries. The 3/8 inch chuck limits bit size, and the platform is meant for occasional use. For hanging pictures, assembling furniture and basic repairs, it is a sensible way to own two tools at a low outlay.

Ownership is minimal. The battery and charger are included, but a single battery means downtime during a long job. Keep the clutch ring clean and avoid heavy use. The 3/8 inch chuck means bits above that size will not fit, so a spade bit for a large door bore needs a different tool. Treat the clutch as a screw-protection device: start at a low number and step up until the screw seats flush.
products.bestFor: Casual homeowners who want the lowest total outlay for two tools.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Brushless motors use electronics instead of carbon brushes, which cuts friction, heat and wear. They give more runtime per charge and a longer life under heavy use. The Milwaukee 2892-22CT and CRAFTSMAN RP kit use brushless motors, while the BLACK+DECKER does not. Buyers who use their tools weekly should pay for brushless. A buyer who shops on price alone often ends up with a kit whose batteries cost more to replace than the tools, which is why the platform check comes first.

Two batteries let you work while one charges, which matters more than a bigger battery for most users. Compact 1.3 to 2.0 Ah packs are light but run out sooner. The Milwaukee, DEWALT DCK277D2 and CRAFTSMAN RP kits all include two. The BLACK+DECKER ships with one, so expect downtime. Test any kit mentally by asking how many holes and screws a typical weekend project needs, then compare that to what a 2.0 Ah pack delivers.

The battery family decides which tools you can add later without buying new packs. M18 and 20V MAX are broad families, while V20 is narrower. Choosing a platform is a five-year decision. Buyers often focus on the kit price and forget the platform cost. The Milwaukee 2892-22CT shows what a compact brushless pair feels like, and that is the benchmark to hold cheaper kits against.

Compact tools fit between studs and under cabinets, but full-size tools offer more power. The DEWALT DCK277D2 measures 7.6 inches front to back, while the Milwaukee is also compact. Lighter tools reduce fatigue on overhead work. A rule of thumb is that the drill and impact driver together should weigh less than 8 pounds with batteries if you work overhead.

A clutch stops the motor at a set torque so screws do not strip, and a chuck holds bits. The BLACK+DECKER drill has 11 clutch positions and a 3/8 inch chuck. Most compact kits use 1/2 inch chucks for larger bits. The DEWALT DCK277D2 and Milwaukee 2892-22CT list compact frames, which is the first spec to compare for tight cabinet work.

UWO is DEWALT's measure of power at the chuck, and the DCK240C2 quotes up to 300. Other brands use torque or RPM. Comparing these across brands is difficult, so use motor type and platform as better guides. Some brands quote torque, some quote UWO and some quote RPM, which is why you cannot rank kits by these numbers alone.

specDecoder.meaning: Unit watts out measures power delivered at the chuck. It is DEWALT's way of describing real output.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 300 UWO on the DCK240C2 is not directly comparable to a Milwaukee torque figure.

specDecoder.meaning: Brushless motors use electronic commutation instead of carbon brushes. This improves efficiency and life.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DCK277D2 listing does not say brushless, so do not assume it.

specDecoder.meaning: 20V MAX is a peak voltage rating of a fresh battery, and nominal voltage is 18V. Both labels describe the same cell count.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 20V MAX DEWALT is not more powerful than an 18V M18 on voltage alone.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp hours measure battery capacity. A 2.0 Ah pack runs about half as long as a 4.0 Ah pack.
specDecoder.watchFor: The CRAFTSMAN and BLACK+DECKER kits use small packs, so expect shorter runtime.

specDecoder.meaning: Clutch rings set the torque at which the drill stops. More positions give finer control.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BLACK+DECKER's 11 positions help beginners, but heavy users rarely use the clutch.

cards.label: Brushless
cards.text: Electronic commutation cuts heat and wear, so batteries last longer and the tool lives longer. The Milwaukee 2892-22CT and CRAFTSMAN V20 RP use it.

cards.label: Brushed or unstated
cards.text: Carbon brushes wear and need replacement, and runtime is shorter. The BLACK+DECKER and DEWALT DCK240C2 do not claim brushless.

howToChoose.note: Pick brushless for weekly use; choose brushed only for occasional jobs.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Renovation means long days, tight spaces and drywall dust. Look for brushless motors, two batteries and compact frames that reach between studs.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Milwaukee 2892-22CT and DEWALT DCK277D2 fit renovation work best. The CRAFTSMAN RP is a lower-cost alternative with brushless motors.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use tools weekly or plan to build a collection. The Milwaukee 2892-22CT and DEWALT DCK277D2 show what the upper end of this cap buys.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use tools a few times a month. The BLACK+DECKER or CRAFTSMAN RP covers that and leaves money for bits.

maintenance.why: Drywall and wood dust gum up jaws and stop them from gripping. A dirty chuck lets bits slip.
Lithium cells age faster when stored full or empty. Half charge indoors is best.
A gritty clutch gives inconsistent torque. Wipe it clean and test it on scrap.
Worn bits slip and strip screws. Use impact-rated bits in the impact driver.
Dirty contacts waste power and heat the pack. A dry cloth is enough.

faq.q: Is a combo kit better than buying tools separately?
faq.a: A kit is usually cheaper than two bare tools plus batteries. If you already own batteries, bare tools are the better deal. Check the platform before deciding. Bundles also include a bag in some cases, which bare tools never do.
It buys a kit with two tools, batteries and a charger, and at the top end brushless motors. Listing prices move, so check the live cost.

faq.q: How long will a kit last?
faq.a: Brushless kits from pro-grade platforms last the longest. Budget kits last for years at light use. Batteries usually wear out first. Charge batteries before storage and avoid leaving them in a hot vehicle, since heat shortens pack life more than use does.
No. The 20V MAX label is a peak rating of a fresh battery. Nominal voltage is 18V.

faq.q: Do I need both a drill and an impact driver?
faq.a: A drill driver handles holes and light driving. An impact driver is better for long screws. Together they cover nearly all household work. Impact drivers are louder, so wear hearing protection during long sessions.

faq.q: Which kit is best for a first-time buyer?
faq.a: The Milwaukee 2892-22CT is the best long-term choice, while the BLACK+DECKER is the cheapest. Pick the one that fits how often you will work.
